wiki: The 2019-2020 season started well for the Lobos, as transfers [[JaQuan Lyle]], J.J. Caldwell, [[Carlton Bragg Jr.]], and Vance Jackson led UNM to a 15–3 start. The Lobos then slumped to 3–11 to finish out the season. Bragg Jr. was accused of sexual assault and later arrested for DWI in January 2020 and was dismissed from the team.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Month by month: A dreary 2020 for sports on most fronts in New Mexico - Albuquerque Journal |url=https://www.abqjournal.com/1530317/a-dreary-year-on-most-fronts-for-preps-unm.html |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=www.abqjournal.com}}</ref> Caldwell was also kicked off the team in January because of a domestic violence accusation.<ref name=":0" /> Also in January, Lyle hosted a party at an [[Airbnb]] location where two people were shot, one of which was a UNM female athlete.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Female UNM athlete shot at NE ABQ party - Albuquerque Journal |url=https://www.abqjournal.com/1413948/female-unm-athlete-shot-at-party-attended-by-numerous-lobos-recruits.html |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=www.abqjournal.com}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2020-01-30 |title=Lobo basketball suspends JaQuan Lyle for house party, shooting incident |url=https://www.krqe.com/news/albuquerque-metro/lobo-basketball-suspends-jaquan-lyle-for-house-party-shooting-incident/ |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=KRQE NEWS 13 - Breaking News, Albuquerque News, New Mexico News, Weather, and Videos |language=en-US}}</ref> It was later revealed that UNM basketball players were also at the party after a 22-point loss to Nevada, after they had taken a charter flight that night.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schutte |first=Chris |date=2020-01-28 |title=A timeline of JaQuan Lyle's wild, tumultuous college basketball journey |url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2020/1/28/21111994/a-timeline-of-jaquan-lyles-wild-tumultuous-college-basketball-journey-new-mexico-basketball-osu |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=Mid-Major Madness |language=en}}</ref> Lyle had not traveled to Nevada because of a knee injury.<ref name=":1" /> UNM would go on to lose in the quarterfinals to Utah State in the [[2020 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West Championship]].

On March 16, 2021, [[Richard Pitino]] was named the 22nd head coach of the Lobos.<ref name=Pitino>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-16 |title=Richard Pitino |url=https://golobos.com/coach/richard-pitino/ |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=University of New Mexico Lobos athletics |language=en-US}}</ref> Pitino inherited 6 transfers, including three former Power-5 league players in [[Jaelen House]], [[Jamal Mashburn Jr.]], and Gethro Muscadin. The Lobos started out 8–6 in the non-conference, including a win against in-state rival [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] where the game was delayed due to a power outage at [[Pan American Center]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-01 |title=New Mexico turns the lights out on New Mexico State in 101-94 rivalry win |url=https://www.ktsm.com/sports/college-sports/nmsu/new-mexico-turns-the-lights-out-on-new-mexico-state-in-101-94-rivalry-win/ |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=KTSM 9 News |language=en-US}}</ref> In Mountain West play, however, the Lobos went 5–12. The highlight of the season was a 75–66 win over No. 22 [[2021–22 Wyoming Cowboys basketball team|Wyoming]]. They went on to lose in the first round in the [[2022 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West Championship]] against [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]].

On March 30, 2025, [[Eric Olen]] was named head coach of the Lobos.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44467550/sources-new-mexico-hire-uc-san-diego-eric-olen-coach ''New Mexico hires UC San Diego's Eric Olen as new coach''], ESPN, March 30, 2025.</ref> Olen was head coach at [[UC San Diego Tritons men's basketball|UC San Diego]] for 12 seasons, the school’s all-time winningest coach, and led the program through the transition from Division II to Division I. The team reached the NCAA Tournament in 2025, the first season the school was eligible, compiling a 30-5 record.<ref name=Olen>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-30 |title=Eric Olen |url=https://golobos.com/sports/mbball/roster/season/2025-26/staff/eric-olen/ |access-date=2026-05-28 |website=University of New Mexico Lobos athletics |language=en-US}}</ref>
